bug-1-dashboard-toast.why: Each reload created the sample dashboard again, which Core's name check refused with an error toast. Fixed in Task 1 before recording: the dashboard is created only when the project has none of that name. On Core (Task 6) the same check goes through Core's dashboardsList.
bug-1-dashboard-toast.expected: No difference: the baseline already shows one sample dashboard and only the "Demo database loaded" toast on each reload.

bug-2-extra-tab.why: addDemoConnection opened a query tab on every load, after the page had restored the project's tabs. Fixed in Task 1 before recording: it opens one only when the project has no query tab.
bug-2-extra-tab.expected: No difference: the baseline already restores the same tabs on each reload.

decision-8-cells.why: Cells cross as Arrow bytes decoded by decode.rs, as on desktop, instead of Arrow-JS toJSON().
decision-8-cells.expected: `created_at` (TIMESTAMP) arrives as DuckDB's text (`2024-01-15 10:30:00`) instead of epoch milliseconds (`1705314600000`), and the grid formats it as a date and time (`Jan 15, 2024, <time>` after normalising), as on desktop. Other sample columns (integers, text) are unchanged.

bug-7-page-sql.decision: Bug 7 (5b: LIMIT on a line of its own)
bug-7-page-sql.why: Core's Dialect::paginate puts LIMIT/OFFSET on a line of its own; duckdb.ts appended it to the statement's last line.
bug-7-page-sql.expected: The error for `SELECT * FROM demo.no_such_table` quotes `LINE 1: SELECT * FROM demo.no_such_table` without ` LIMIT 101 OFFSET 0` (the `pane` of the destructive step still shows that error, since a deferred run shows nothing new). The message also starts with `Query failed: `: Core's error wording, as desktop (`DbError::query` in `seaquel-types`).

q6-edit-sql.decision: Q6 A (Core's behaviour); Decision 9; 5c's edits service
q6-edit-sql.why: Core plans the edit (db.planEdits) and keeps its binds; the browser driver writes them as typed literals only when it runs the statement (Decision 9). The TS service inlined values into the SQL it showed.
q6-edit-sql.expected: The apply confirmation shows Core's SQL with `?` placeholders for the value and key instead of `= 'Jonson' WHERE "id" = 1`; the sheet's SQL view gains the "Values: …" line. The grid before and after the apply is unchanged apart from decision-8-cells.

q6-data-tab.decision: Q6 A; bug 7 (filters bound, count only when needed); Decision 9
q6-data-tab.why: The data tab's query is Core's build_table_select with bound filter values, and its count runs only for a full page.
q6-data-tab.expected: No visible difference for this filter: the same three rows, `3 rows` and `Showing 1-3 of 3 rows` (the page isn't full, so no estimate). Listed so the probe knows the path changed.

q7-ai-hidden.why: features.aiAssistant is false in the demo (Task 6). Before Task 6 the flag was defined (features/index.ts) and read nowhere; Task 6 wires it through aiSettingsStore.available, which the header's toggle, the command palette's Toggle AI item, the editor's inline prompt, the right panel and Settings' AI group read, and gates the Features section's AI switch.
q7-ai-hidden.expected: The header has no "Toggle AI Assistant" button. In the `grid edit, pending changes off` step's `settings` (Settings → Features), the AI feature switch is gone and the sidebar has no AI group; the AI provider and privacy sections aren't shown in the all-settings view. Not in the recording but gone too: the command palette's Toggle AI item and the editor's inline AI prompt.

history-survives-reload.decision: Task 6 (Task 1's finding: today's demo loses its query history on a reload); Decision 19
history-survives-reload.why: The demo connection's history now comes from storage: the page loads it with the saved connections, and addDemoConnection keeps it instead of resetting it to [].
history-survives-reload.expected: `final reload`'s queries panel shows `History 4` (the {{param}} run, the DELETE … WHERE id = 1, the count and the applied grid UPDATE) instead of `History 0`, and the last step shows `History 6` instead of 2. The applied grid edit is listed with its `?` placeholders and no values: applied edits are stored that way on every interface (a cross-interface follow-up in the plan).
